### 1. path-boundary-link-swap-toctou

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | `ClientRootPathValidator.ValidatePathAgainstRootsAsync` (`src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ClientRootPathValidator.cs:40-64`) computes a fully link-resolved canonical target internally (`ValidatePath` → `ResolvePath` at line 81, delegating to `ConfiguredRootBoundary.ResolvePath`, `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Security/ConfiguredRootBoundary.cs:104-118`, which walks every path component and resolves symlinks/junctions before comparison) but returns `Task` — the canonical string is discarded. The highest-risk direct-write caller, `EditTools.ApplyTextEdit` (`src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/EditTools.cs:32-33`), validates the client-supplied `filePath`, then passes that SAME raw (possibly-symlinked) string into `editService.ApplyTextEditsAsync`. The physical write happens in `EditService.PersistDocumentTextToDiskAsync` (`src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/EditService.cs:700-731`), which re-derives the write target from `document.FilePath` — a value looked up via a purely lexical `Path.GetFullPath` match (`SymbolResolver.FindDocument`, `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Helpers/SymbolResolver.cs:518-524`), NOT link-resolved — and passes it straight to `AtomicFileWriter.WriteAllTextAsync`, which re-walks the filesystem path at write time. If an attacker swaps a symlink/junction component of the original path between the `ValidatePathAgainstRootsAsync` call and this OS-level write, the bytes land at the swapped (now out-of-boundary) target even though validation passed. This is the exact gap the item's Evidence describes ("validation currently canonicalizes only for comparison and returns no canonical target"). Diagnosis correction: the item's Anchors also cite `ProjectMutationTools.cs`, but that file never calls `ClientRootPathValidator` — it resolves `projectName` against documents already loaded in the workspace snapshot, not a raw client-supplied filesystem path, so it is not a participant in this specific link-swap vector and needed no code change here (retained only as background in the item). No Rule 1 bundling applies (`bundleCandidatePeers` empty). |
| Approach | (1) `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ClientRootPathValidator.cs`: change `ValidatePathAgainstRootsAsync` to return `Task<string>` — the already-computed canonical target — instead of `Task`. `ConfiguredRootBoundary.cs` needs no change; its `ResolvePath` already does correct link-walking canonicalization. (2) `src/RoslynMcp.Core/Services/IEditService.cs`: add a trailing optional parameter `string? canonicalWritePath = null` to `ApplyTextEditsAsync` (after `autoRevertOnError`) — default `null` preserves behavior for every other caller. (3) `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/EditService.cs`: thread `canonicalWritePath` through `ApplyTextEditsAsync` → `ApplyTextEditsCoreAsync` → `PersistDocumentTextToDiskAsync`; when non-null, write via `AtomicFileWriter.WriteAllTextAsync(canonicalWritePath, …)` instead of `document.FilePath` — closing the OS-level re-walk gap — while leaving `document`-based lookup and encoding detection (lines 703-706, 718) untouched, deliberately, to avoid regressing legitimate document resolution for workspaces loaded through a symlinked project directory (MSBuildWorkspace does not itself canonicalize `Document.FilePath` through links, so reusing the canonical form for lookup risked false misses). (4) `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/EditTools.cs`: `apply_text_edit` captures the `Task<string>` result from `ValidatePathAgainstRootsAsync(server, filePath, c)` and passes it as `canonicalWritePath`. Mirrors the existing "carry the canonical validated target into the write" strategy the acceptance criteria names as the preferred option over per-call revalidation. |
| Scope | Production files (4, within the Rule 3 base cap — no exemption claimed): `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ClientRootPathValidator.cs` (return canonical path), `src/RoslynMcp.Core/Services/IEditService.cs` (new optional parameter), `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/EditService.cs` (thread + use canonical path at the physical write), `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/EditTools.cs` (`apply_text_edit` consumer). Test files (3, within the Rule 4 cap): `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/ClientRootPathValidatorTests.cs` (canonical-return assertions), `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/ExpandedSurfaceIntegrationTests.cs` (new deterministic link-swap regression, acceptance item 4), `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/SuppressionServiceTests.cs` (gate-forced companion touch: `StubEditService`/`ApplyToDiskEditService`, the only two other `IEditService` implementers besides `EditService` itself — verified via `symbol_search` — must add the new interface parameter to compile; no behavior change). |

Closing it requires canonicalizing document paths at workspace-load time — a different seam (`WorkspaceManager`, an addenda-declared hotspot) with its own false-miss risk for workspaces legitimately loaded through a symlinked project directory. ### 2. type-extraction-member-shape-validation

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | Three distinct unsafe-shape bugs confirmed in `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/TypeExtractionService.cs`. (1) `GetMemberName` (line 449-460) maps `ConstructorDeclarationSyntax c => c.Identifier.Text` — a constructor's identifier is always the source type's name, so a requested member name matching it gets selected by `PartitionMembers` (line 129-169) and emitted unchanged inside `public sealed class {newTypeName}` by `BuildNewFileRoot`/`EnsurePublicAccessibility` (neither of which retargets a constructor identifier), producing an ill-formed "method" with the OLD type's name inside the NEW type (CS1520-class breakage). (2) `GetMemberName`'s `FieldDeclarationSyntax` case (line 455) returns only `f.Declaration.Variables.FirstOrDefault()?.Identifier.Text` — the first declarator's name. `PartitionMembers`'s single foreach (line 136-148) then matches/moves the WHOLE multi-declarator field as one node keyed off that first name: requesting `"a"` from `private int a, b, c;` silently drags `b`/`c` along; requesting `"b"` or `"c"` alone never matches at all and both stay behind with no signal to the caller. (3) `PartitionMembers`'s `memberNameSet.Remove(name)` (line 142) fires on the first source-order match; for an overloaded method the first-declared overload is extracted and the name is removed from the set, so every later same-named overload silently falls through to `toKeep` — the caller never learns a choice was made on their behalf. |
| Approach | All edits confined to `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/TypeExtractionService.cs`. Restructure `PartitionMembers` into a validate-then-partition shape: (1) **Pre-pass refusal**, before the extract/keep split — build a lookup of method-overload groups keyed by `GetMemberName` (methods only); for any requested name resolving to >1 `MethodDeclarationSyntax`, throw `ExtractTypeBlockingDependencyException` with one `BlockingDependencyDto` per candidate (`member=name`, `reason` citing the candidate's `ParameterList` signature and instructing the caller to target one overload or split the extraction). For any requested name resolving to a `ConstructorDeclarationSyntax`, throw the same exception type with a reason stating constructors are never eligible for extraction. Both reuse the existing structured-refusal shape already used for unmatched names at line 150-163 — same exception type, same `BlockingDependencyDto`, so callers get one consistent contract instead of a third ad hoc shape. (2) **Field-declarator-aware partition** — add a helper (e.g. `GetFieldDeclaratorNames`) that returns ALL declarator names for a `FieldDeclarationSyntax`, not just the first. When a multi-declarator field has only SOME declarators requested, split it into two `FieldDeclarationSyntax` nodes via `.WithDeclaration(declaration.WithVariables(...))` — one holding only the requested `VariableDeclaratorSyntax`(s) (goes to `toExtract`), one holding the rest (goes to `toKeep`) — both preserving the original type, modifiers, and attributes. When ALL declarators of a field are requested, keep the existing single-node move (already safe). (3) Keep the existing unmatched-name refusal (line 150-163) as the final check, now operating over the extended per-declarator name set. No `ITypeExtractionService` signature change — `memberNames` stays a flat string list; the acceptance criterion's "require an explicit all-overloads selection" alternative is not pursued because plain refusal is the smaller, root-cause-correct fix that stays inside the 1-file/S-size budget (Directive #6). |
| Scope | Production files (1): `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/TypeExtractionService.cs`. Test files (1, extended, not new): `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/TypeExtractionTests.cs`. No Rule 3 exemption needed. |
| Tool policy | edit-only |
| Estimated context cost | 35000 |
| Risks | **Fanout probe (Rule 5b) — measured `fanoutEstimate: 1`, matching `productionFilesTouched: 1`.** This is not a refactor-shaped change (no rename, no signature change, no cross-cutting edit): `PartitionMembers` and `GetMemberName` are `private static` and referenced only from within `TypeExtractionService.cs`. Probe method: repo-wide grep for `GetMemberName\|PartitionMembers` across `src/`, which returned 11 hits across 3 files; the 2 files other than `TypeExtractionService.cs` — `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/ClassSplitOrchestrator.cs:100` and `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/SymbolRefactorService.cs:1666` — each declare their OWN independent `private static string? GetMemberName(MemberDeclarationSyntax)` and are not callers of the edited symbols, so they are excluded from the blast radius. Distinct-file blast radius after exclusion: 1. Adjacent duplication observed (not in scope, no shared code path with this file — Rule 1 does not bundle): those same two private `GetMemberName` copies carry the identical first-declarator-only field naming and no constructor/overload guard — worth a follow-up backlog row auditing those two services for the same bug class. Field-split must preserve initializers/attributes/modifiers exactly on both halves — cover with a fixture that has an initializer on a retained (non-extracted) declarator. The new overload-ambiguity refusal must not misfire on genuinely single-declaration names — verify no regression on the existing single-method extraction tests (e.g. `ExtractType_NoExternalConsumers_ProducesPreview`). |
| Validation | `mcp__roslyn__compile_check` on `TypeExtractionService.cs` after the edit. Add 3 new `[TestMethod]`s to `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/TypeExtractionTests.cs`, mirroring the fixture-based pattern at `ExtractType_OverrideMember_StripsOverrideFromNewType` (line 440+): `ExtractType_ConstructorRequested_RefusesWithStructuredBlockingDependency` (fixture whose ctor name is passed in `memberNames`; assert `ExtractTypeBlockingDependencyException` with a `BlockingDependencies` entry naming the ctor); `ExtractType_MultiDeclaratorField_SplitsOnlyRequestedVariables` (fixture `private int a, b;`, request only `"a"`; assert the new-type diff contains `a` and not `b`, and the source diff still declares `b`); `ExtractType_AmbiguousOverload_RefusesWithStructuredCandidates` (fixture with two `Foo(...)` overloads, request `"Foo"`; assert `ExtractTypeBlockingDependencyException` with >=2 `BlockingDependencies` entries). Run targeted `TypeExtractionTests` (all methods, not just the 3 new ones — confirm no regression on `ExtractType_OverrideMember_StripsOverrideFromNewType`, `ExtractType_NewMember_StripsNewModifierFromNewType`, `ExtractType_MemberNotFound_ThrowsWithStructuredBlockingDependencies`, etc.). Full `./eng/verify-release.ps1 -Configuration Release` per addenda `ci_equivalent` before shipping. |
| Performance review | N/A — correctness fix, no hot-path changes (preview-only code path, invoked once per extract-type request, not in a loop). |
| CHANGELOG category | Fixed |
| CHANGELOG entry (draft) | Fixed: `extract_type` preview now refuses unsafe extraction member shapes — a source-type constructor named in `memberNames` is refused instead of being emitted unchanged into the new type, a multi-declarator field is split so only the requested variables move (unrequested siblings are never silently dragged along), and an ambiguous method-overload name is refused with the candidate signatures listed instead of silently picking the first-declared overload by source order. |
| Backlog sync | Close rows: [type-extraction-member-shape-validation]. |

### 3. elicitation-inflight-cancellation-test-harness-deadlock

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | The awaited call is `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Elicitation/ElicitationChoicePrompt.cs:123` (`result = await server.ElicitAsync(request, cancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false)`), whose surrounding try/catch (120-140) deliberately does NOT catch `OperationCanceledException` (elicitation-trychoice-cancellation-swallow) so cancellation propagates. Per this row's own Evidence, a prior attempt additionally wrapped this in `.AsTask().WaitAsync(cancellationToken)` and the genuinely-in-flight repro STILL deadlocked — that rules out "outer await doesn't observe the token" as the cause; the block is upstream of this line. The regression harness is `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/Helpers/InMemoryMcpClientServerHarness.cs:54-76`: two `System.IO.Pipelines.Pipe` instances (`clientToServer`, `serverToClient`), each exposed via `.AsStream()`, drive a real `StreamServerTransport`/`StreamClientTransport` pair with `server.RunAsync(serverCancellation.Token)` running as a background `Task` (`serverRunTask`, line 76) for the harness's lifetime, all inside ONE test process. ### 7. group-c-compilation-cache-gate-hardening

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | Root cause confirmed at `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Helpers/SymbolResolver.cs:51-68` (`CanUseCompilationCache`), `:175` (`FindClosestMatchesAsync`), `:353` (`ResolveByMetadataNameAsync`), `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Helpers/SymbolHandleSerializer.cs:213` (`FindAllByMetadataNameAsync`), and `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/CompilationCache.cs:70-72` (`GetCompilationAsync`). Each of the three static helpers computes `var useCache = CanUseCompilationCache(solution, compilationCache, workspaceId)` ONCE before its `foreach (var project in solution.Projects)` loop, but `CompilationCache.GetCompilationAsync` re-reads `_workspaceManager.GetCurrentVersion(workspaceId)` on EVERY call and keys purely on `(workspaceId, ProjectId, version)`. A mid-loop workspace reload/version bump therefore causes the cache to compute-and-STORE a compilation built from the pre-bump `Project` instance under the NEW version key — poisoning the cache for every later caller reading that project at the new version until the next bump. Separately (2026-08-10 amendment), `CanUseCompilationCache`'s liveness check `ReferenceEquals(solution, solution.Workspace.CurrentSolution)` only proves liveness w.r.t. the solution's OWN `Workspace` back-reference — it never confirms that back-reference IS the workspace registered under the caller-supplied `workspaceId`. A live solution from workspace B passed with `workspaceId: "A"` passes the gate today and would pollute A's cache slot; the XML doc's claim that the check is "semantically `solution == IWorkspaceManager.GetCurrentSolution(workspaceId)`" is currently false. `bundleCandidatePeers` was empty — `ruleOneBundleResolved: n/a`, single-row initiative. |
| Approach | (1) `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Contracts/ICompilationCache.cs` — add `bool IsLiveSolution(string workspaceId, Solution solution)`: "is `solution` reference-equal to the CURRENT live solution `IWorkspaceManager` reports for `workspaceId`" — the check the doc comment already claims exists. (2) `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/CompilationCache.cs` — implement `IsLiveSolution` using the already-injected `_workspaceManager.GetCurrentSolution(workspaceId)`, catching `StaleWorkspaceTransitionException` (the exception `GetCurrentSolution` throws during a reload-transition/disposed-snapshot window — mirrors the old `CanUseCompilationCache`'s `ObjectDisposedException` catch) and returning `false` to degrade to the raw fetch instead of throwing out of a read-side helper. (3) `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Helpers/SymbolResolver.cs` — rewrite `CanUseCompilationCache` to delegate to `cache.IsLiveSolution(workspaceId, solution)` instead of the self-referential check (closes the identity gap); add a new `internal static Task<Compilation?> GetProjectCompilationAsync(Solution solution, Project project, ICompilationCache? compilationCache, string? workspaceId, CancellationToken ct)` that calls `CanUseCompilationCache` FRESH on every invocation (not hoisted) — the single shared fetch-dispatch site acceptance bullet 3 asks for; replace the hoisted `useCache` bool + inline ternary in both `FindClosestMatchesAsync` (`:175`/`:181-183`) and `ResolveByMetadataNameAsync` (`:353`/`:357-359`) with a call to `GetProjectCompilationAsync` inside the loop, so the gate is re-evaluated per project iteration; add `internal static void ValidateCacheParameters(ICompilationCache? compilationCache, string? workspaceId)` throwing `ArgumentException(nameof(workspaceId))` when `compilationCache is not null && string.IsNullOrEmpty(workspaceId)`, called once at the top of both public methods (before the loop, so an empty-project solution still fails loudly); revise the `CanUseCompilationCache` XML remarks to describe the corrected workspaceId-scoped semantics. (4) `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Helpers/SymbolHandleSerializer.cs` — `FindAllByMetadataNameAsync` calls `SymbolResolver.ValidateCacheParameters(...)` once at the top and replaces its own hoisted `useCache` (`:213`) + inline ternary (`:219-220`) with `await SymbolResolver.GetProjectCompilationAsync(solution, project, compilationCache, workspaceId, ct)`. |
| Scope | Production files (4, at the Rule 3 cap, no exemption needed): `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Contracts/ICompilationCache.cs`, `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/CompilationCache.cs`, `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Helpers/SymbolResolver.cs`, `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Helpers/SymbolHandleSerializer.cs`. Test files (1, extends existing, within Rule 4): `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/CompilationCacheAdoptionTests.cs` — (a) implement the new `IsLiveSolution` member on this file's two existing `ICompilationCache` test doubles (`CountingAdhocCompilationCache`, `RecordingCompilationCache` — the latter delegates to `_inner.IsLiveSolution(...)`), a mechanical companion forced by the interface addition; (b) add 3 new `[TestMethod]`s covering the three acceptance bullets (see Validation). Grep confirmed exactly 3 repo-wide implementers of `ICompilationCache` (`CompilationCache`, and the two test doubles above) — all covered by this Scope, so the interface addition introduces no missed companion touch. |
| Tool policy | edit-only |
| Estimated context cost | 55000 |
| Risks | The `IsLiveSolution` interface addition is a breaking change to `ICompilationCache`, confirmed to have exactly 3 implementers repo-wide via `Grep ": ICompilationCache"` — all 3 are in this initiative's touched-file set (fanoutEstimate: 4, matches productionFilesTouched, within tolerance). `CompilationCache.IsLiveSolution` calls `_workspaceManager.GetCurrentSolution(workspaceId)`, which throws for a genuinely unknown `workspaceId` — pre-existing behavior (the unconditional `GetCurrentVersion(workspaceId)` call already at the top of `GetCompilationAsync` assumes a valid id today), so no new failure mode; only the reload-transition (`StaleWorkspaceTransitionException`) window is caught and degrades to the raw fetch. Still unreachable in production today per the item's Context — no caller passes `compilationCache`/`workspaceId` into these 3 helpers yet (confirmed via Grep: only test callers do); this is pre-consumer hardening, and the sibling row `compilation-cache-wire-group-c-consumer` should re-verify that assumption before wiring the first real caller. The redesigned `CanUseCompilationCache` must NOT regress the existing `MigratedHelpers_ForkedSolution_DoNotRouteThroughCache` test's hard-zero-cache-call-count contract for a forked (never-applied) solution — verified by re-running it, not just adding new tests. |

### 10. filewatcher-clearstale-timeout-flake-triage

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | `ExternalEditStalenessTests.cs:405` (`await parked.WaitAsync(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(UnblockBoundMs))`) bounds the test's pass/fail on a 10,000ms wall-clock window (already widened once from 2000ms — see the doc comment at lines 347-355) around observing the parked awaiter transition to Canceled after `ClearStale`. The production code is already correct: `FileWatcherService.cs:255-274` (`Entry.ClearStale`) calls `_staleSignal.TrySetCanceled()` synchronously under `_reasonLock`, on the calling thread, before `ClearStale()` returns — so the TCS's `Task.IsCanceled`/`IsCompleted` **state** transitions synchronously with that call. `TaskCreationOptions.RunContinuationsAsynchronously` (set at `FileWatcherService.cs:194-195` and `272`) only defers scheduling of registered *continuations* (the code after an `await`) — it does not delay the synchronous `IsCompleted`/`IsCanceled` property reads. The test's `await parked.WaitAsync(...)` forces a continuation onto the thread pool and is exactly the mechanism vulnerable to scheduling delay under self-hosted-runner load: that is the actual root cause of the registered flake, not a defect in `FileWatcherService`. No Rule 1 bundling applies — `bundleCandidatePeers` is empty. |
| Approach | In `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/ExternalEditStalenessTests.cs`, replace the `await parked.WaitAsync(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(UnblockBoundMs))` try/catch block (lines 403-412) with a direct, synchronous check of `parked.IsCompleted` / `parked.IsCanceled` read immediately after `watcher.ClearStale(workspaceId)` returns — no `await`, no timer, nothing for host scheduling load to slip past. Update the two `Assert.IsTrue` failure messages (currently referencing the elapsed bound) to describe the synchronous check instead. Remove the now-unused `UnblockBoundMs` constant (line 356) and its doc comment (lines 347-355). Retain ONE generous defense-in-depth `await parked.WaitAsync(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30))` (matching `awaiterCts`'s own 30s deadline) purely as a hang-guard so a genuinely-stranded awaiter still fails the run instead of hanging it forever — but that await must not gate the pass/fail assertion itself, which is the synchronous check above. Then remove the `FileWatcherClearStaleAwaiterTests...` row from `ai_docs/known-flakes.md`'s Registered-flakes table per Acceptance criterion 2, once the rewritten test is confirmed deterministic (see Validation). |

Test files: 1 modified (`tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/ExternalEditStalenessTests.cs`). Documentation: 1 modified (`ai_docs/known-flakes.md` — remove the resolved flake row). No Rule 3 exemption needed (0 production files touched). |

For a marketplace-plugin consumer none of those literals exist in the tool surface, so the gate hard-stops a legitimate install. **Why the parent was blocked and why this seam:** the parent bundled the genericity-guard tightening (an assertion that no gate-carrying file contains a bare literal) with content fixes.
